conventions.hf_hidden_states: Verified empirically (transformers 5.12.1): hidden_states[0] = input to block 0 (embeddings; for CLIP after pre_layrnorm); hidden_states[i] = output of 0-based block i-1 = 1-based block i; no final LayerNorm in any hidden_states entry. last_hidden_state = final LayerNorm(hidden_states[-1]) for DINOv2 and SigLIP; for CLIP last_hidden_state == hidden_states[24] (post_layernorm only acts on the pooled CLS token).
conventions.block_numbering_in_this_project: sweep 'L<k>' and the paper's layer analysis use the HF index = 1-based block k; xSoyelNet-ML / ab M6 / M610 and DeepGaze MSDB 'blocks 6 and 10' are 0-based (= HF hidden_states[7], [11] = 1-based blocks 7 and 11). So sweep 'block 6' (hidden_states[6]) and xSoyelNet-ML's 'block 6' (hidden_states[7]) are different tensors.
conventions.pre_vs_post_ln: xSoyelNet-ASPP and ab/readout_A/B read last_hidden_state (after the final LayerNorm); every sweep readout and M6/M610 read hidden_states (before it).
conventions.deepgaze_layernorm: DeepGaze LayerNorm normalises over (C, H, W) per image, i.e. with image-wide statistics, so DeepGaze's 1x1 readout is pointwise in its convolutions but not in its normalisation.
conventions.rf_units: theoretical receptive fields are in pixels of the backbone input; DeepGaze IIE backbones see the display at half resolution, so display px = 2 x

iie_feature_set_for_readout_swap.recommendation: DeepGaze IIE backbone 1: RGBShapeNetC (torchvision ResNet-50 trained on Stylized-ImageNet + ImageNet, fine-tuned on ImageNet), layers layer3.0.conv2, layer3.3.conv2, layer3.5.conv1, layer3.5.conv2 (256 ch each, stride 16), layer4.1.conv2, layer4.2.conv2 (512 ch each, stride 32); 2,048 channels
reasons: cheapest on CPU: 0.15 s per 512 x 384 forward with 3 threads (EfficientNet-B5 0.89 s, DenseNet-201 0.23 s, ResNeXt-50 0.19 s)

documented, standard torchvision module names (deepgaze2e.py BACKBONES entry 1) and weights already cached locally; IIE's own trained readout for exactly these features is in deepgaze2e.pth (models.0.*, 30 components), so R1 can be compared with IIE's own weights

smallest and finite theoretical receptive fields (107, 203, 235, 267, 363, 427 px of the backbone input), needed for an analysis of units whose receptive field excludes every inducer; EfficientNet-B5 has squeeze-excitation (global gating) in every block and DenseNet-201's hooked layers have a 3,799 px receptive field (global)
no global operation inside the backbone up to the hooked layers (pure conv / BN / ReLU / max-pool), so any global context in a readout test comes from the readout
iie_feature_set_for_readout_swap.caveat: IIE feeds the backbone a half-resolution image; layer4 maps (stride 32) are nearest-upsampled to the stride-16 grid before concatenation
